headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can egress allowlisted data while the zoomcamp repo is read-only, creating modest leakage and workflow-conflict risks; no direct prompt-injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a has no io_surfaces and no network egress, while agent_b only shows allowlisted egress and browser use; nothing indicates agent_a outputs are ingested by agent_b by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later pipes agent_a output into agent_b prompts or browser inputs, reassess injection risk.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Do not copy agent_a output into agent_b prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, while agent_b touches documents/images and can egress to allowlisted APIs. There is no shared workspace or sensitive class documented, so leakage is limited and not default-dangerous. The main risk is accidental document content exposure if the pair is later connected to the same files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same document workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is given sensitive documents, its allowlisted egress can transmit content externally.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of agent_b inputs.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing documents.
Redact documents before OCR.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is a non-runnable course repo with no requested permissions, while agent_b is a runnable document processor with browser and allowlisted network egress. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is not shown. Uncertainty remains because agent_b's filesystem write scope is unspecified, so the safer low rating is chosen.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF agent_b is configured to modify shared git state, contention becomes plausible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git branches.
Run one agent at a time for writes.
Check for hidden write permissions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can process documents and browser content, but agent_a is a course repo rather than an action-taking system or fact source with downstream authority. There is no evidence that agent_b treats agent_a outputs as authoritative, so a cascading-error chain is weak. The uncertainty about any orchestration layer keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are later fed into agent_b as authoritative instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-act on extracted text, errors can propagate further.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs.
Do not auto-ingest agent_a text into agent_b.
Add validation checks before downstream actions.
Log provenance for any transformed output.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented. agent_a lists no data classes touched and no egress, while agent_b handles documents/images with allowlisted egress but no stated regulated-data scope, certifications, or retention mismatch. With only docs-only evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in deployment, reassess.
mitigations: Classify inputs before use.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings.
Confirm deployment region and DPA status.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
